disclosures.name: TestAllocationsFromBytes/Atoi
disclosures.reason: want-zero AllocsPerRun assert: the closure's string([]byte) argument is proven non-escaping by Go's compiler and stays on the stack; the managed model must materialize an @string per run RELABEL 2026-09-23 (C1, from the i7 reading run at bb54ff0920, Release with tiering off): alloc-profile -> deferred. The run's own unit note is COUNT, so golib's counter SAW these objects -- the COUNT arm of the 2026-09-05 ladder -- and the site family is one a named plan removes: string-conversion intermediates. Read at Atoi (src/core/strconv/atoi.cs:255-267): the test's string(bytes.Number) argument, the function-local `"Atoi"u8` constant materialised per call, and `range []byte(s)` copied through slice<byte>(s) -- three conversions Go performs without a heap object, which is Atoi's reading of 3. Only Atoi was decomposed; the other nine share the argument site.
disclosures.reading: 3 per run -- 300 go2cs-runtime object allocations (11,200 bytes) counted over 100 runs at bb54ff0920 (the batch-8b stamp), Release with tiering off -- the i7 reading run, claude/coord-h10-readings ac9f8251ee, docs/phase4/h10-evidence/i7-readings/readings-go1.24.13.tsv; the host's unit note is COUNT, a LOWER BOUND; the test printed `got 3 allocs, want 0 allocs`
disclosures.plan: the string-conversion family -- an intermediate buffer Go never allocates for a conversion whose result is not retained: golib's builtin.tmpstring (the zero-copy transient @string the converter already emits for a map-READ key, docs/ConversionStrategies-Reference.md `m[string(b)]`) extended to a string(b) that the callee or comparison does not retain, with docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-byte-window.md as the converter-side recognition record. The family's other arms, read at Atoi: a function-local string constant hoisted like the literals of docs/phase4/DESIGN-string-literal-allocation.md (Tier C), and `range []byte(s)` walked over the string's bytes without a copy, as Go's compiler does.Retires when a run reads 0 per run with the counter still charging the path; a reading at the want with the counter charging NOTHING is the byte arm (testing.AllocsPerRun's fallback) and would be a false retire.
